title: Algebraic stacks over a scheme viewed over the integers
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with structure morphism $S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Use algebraic stacks [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], categories fibred in groupoids, their morphisms, $2$-morphisms and $2$-fibre products [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], and quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of stacks and of their morphisms [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. For a category fibred in groupoids $p:\mathcal X\to\mathit{Sch}/S$ let $j_!\mathcal X$ be the same category regarded over $\mathit{Sch}/\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ through the functor sending an $S$-scheme $T\to S$ to the scheme $T$; it carries the morphism $j_!\mathcal X\to S$ sending an object over $T\to S$ to that structure map. Then: (1) if $\mathcal X$ is an algebraic stack over $S$, then $j_!\mathcal X$ is an algebraic stack over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, and a smooth surjective scheme atlas $U\to\mathcal X$ remains a smooth surjective scheme atlas of $j_!\mathcal X$ with $U$ regarded as a scheme; (2) $\mathcal X\mapsto(j_!\mathcal X,\,j_!\mathcal X\to S)$ is an equivalence of $2$-categories from algebraic stacks over $S$ to pairs consisting of an algebraic stack over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and a morphism from it to $S$, and $j_!$ carries $2$-fibre products of algebraic stacks over $S$ to $2$-fibre products over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$; (3) an algebraic stack $\mathcal X$ over $S$ is quasi-compact if and only if $j_!\mathcal X$ is, and a morphism $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of algebraic stacks over $S$ is quasi-compact, respectively quasi-separated, over $S$ if and only if $j_!f$ is so over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. For algebraic stacks $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ over $S$, the product $\mathcal X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathcal Y$ means $j_!\mathcal X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}j_!\mathcal Y$, and the absolute diagonal of $\mathcal X$ is the diagonal of the structure morphism $j_!\mathcal X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. No hypothesis on $S$ is imposed.

source.place: Section section-change-base-scheme: Tag 04X5 (lemma-category-of-spaces-over-smaller-base-scheme) and Tag 04X6 (definition-viewed-as), with $S'=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$; its use in stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 050M (lemma-compose-after-separated), proof of (5)-(8), 'think of X and Y as algebraic stacks over Spec(Z)'.

proof.text: Put $B=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Apply [lem-sfb-etale-stack-localization] with $S'=B$. This identifies etale stacks over $S$ with etale stacks over $B$ equipped with a map to $h_S$, by the very same total category and projection specified in the statement. It also identifies functors and natural isomorphisms compatible with that map. It remains to check algebraicity and the geometric predicates; the localization lemma alone asserts none of those.

source.place: Tag 04X5, first paragraph of proof, applying stacks.tex Tag 04WV

proof.text: For the forward diagonal test, let $T\to j_!\mathcal X\times_B j_!\mathcal X$ specify objects $x,y$ with possibly different structure maps $a,b:T\to S$. Form the scheme $E=T\times_{S\times_B S}S$ using $(a,b)$ and the diagonal of $S$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. A map $V\to T$ factors through $E$ exactly when $a|_V=b|_V$. An isomorphism $x|_V\cong y|_V$ in the absolute fibre groupoid forces this equality, since its image in $h_S(V)$ is an identity. Thus the absolute Isom functor over $T$ is the relative Isom functor of $x|_E,y|_E$, composed with $E\to T$. By the representable-diagonal clause of [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], the latter is equivalent over $E$ to an algebraic space $Z$ over $S$ with a map $Z\to h_E$. Apply clause (1) of [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] to $S\to B$: $j_!Z$ is an algebraic space over $B$, and $j_!Z\to h_E\to h_T$ gives its map to $T$. Its points over a $B$-scheme $V\to T$ are the $S$-structures on $V$ together with points of $Z$, which is the absolute Isom functor just described. This proves the absolute diagonal is representable. The functor-of-points description gives the identification on arrows as well. The equalizer scheme $E$ need not be open or closed.

source.place: Tag 04X5, algebraicity check; direct diagonal verification using spaces.tex Tags 03I4 and 04SG

proof.text: For any map $h_T\to j_!\mathcal X$, the map to $h_S$ equips $T$ with its unique indicated $S$-structure. For a scheme map $U\to\mathcal X$, the fibre groupoid of $T\times_{j_!\mathcal X}U$ consists of the same triples and arrows as $T\times_{\mathcal X}U$ over that $S$-structure [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. If it is represented by an algebraic space $Z$, [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] regards $Z$ over either base. Its etale scheme charts and their maps to $T$ are the same: forgetting the $S$-map changes no scheme morphism, and conversely a chart over $Z$ inherits that map. Hence smoothness and surjectivity of $Z\to T$ in [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack] are identical tests. This proves that a smooth surjective scheme atlas over $S$ remains one over $B$. Conversely any such atlas $U\to\mathcal G$ for a stack with a map $\mathcal G\to h_S$ equips $U$ with an $S$-map, and the same reasoning regards it as an atlas over $S$.

source.place: Tag 04X5, preservation of presentations in both constructions; spaces.tex Tag 04SG

proof.text: For the converse diagonal test, start with an algebraic stack $\mathcal G$ over $B$ equipped with $q:\mathcal G\to h_S$. If $x,y$ are objects over the same $S$-scheme $T$, every isomorphism between them over $T$ is automatically over $S$, because $h_S(T)$ has only identity arrows. The absolute diagonal supplies their Isom algebraic space with its map to $T$. Use [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] for $S\to B$ to regard that space, with its composite map to $S$, over $S$; it is exactly the relative Isom space over $T$. Together with the converse atlas check and the stack property from step 1, this proves algebraicity over $S$ by [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. The equivalence in step 1 consequently restricts to the full $2$-categories of algebraic stacks, proving clause (2)'s equivalence and completing clause (1).

source.place: Tag 04X5, converse construction and restriction to algebraic stacks

proof.text: Consider a diagram $\mathcal X\xrightarrow{f}\mathcal Z\xleftarrow{g}\mathcal Y$ over $S$. Over a $B$-scheme $T$, an object of the absolute pullback is a triple $(x,y,\alpha:f(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}g(y))$ [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Its isomorphism $\alpha$ forces the two $S$-structures of $T$ to agree. Hence this is precisely an object of the relative pullback for that common $S$-structure, and the compatibility equation on arrows is unchanged. This gives the canonical equivalence of the two $2$-fibre products, with both projections. This claim concerns pullbacks over $\mathcal Z$; it does not assert preservation of a terminal object or replacement of a product over $S$ by a product over $B$.

source.place: Tag 04X5 and constructions A/B; explicit fibre-product computation

proof.text: By step 3 the very same scheme atlases are allowed over the two bases. Their source schemes have the same underlying spaces, so a quasi-compact source is quasi-compact over either base. The stack quasi-compactness predicate of [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism] is therefore invariant. For a map $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$, every absolute quasi-compact algebraic test stack $\mathcal V\to j_!\mathcal Y$ inherits a map to $S$ by composition, and step 4 regards it as an algebraic stack over $S$. Conversely every relative test gives an absolute one. Step 5 identifies their pullbacks, whose quasi-compactness has just been identified. The universal test in the definition of a quasi-compact morphism is thus the same in both directions.

source.place: Tag 050U (definition-quasi-compact), with the atlas convention of stacks-properties.tex Tag 04YC(3)

proof.text: The corresponding assertion for algebraic spaces follows directly from [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers]: its equivalence carries etale scheme charts to the same charts in both directions, so the existence of a quasi-compact scheme chart is unchanged. For a morphism $A\to C$ of spaces, every quasi-compact absolute test space mapping to $j_!C$ inherits its $S$-map and corresponds to a relative test. The fibre-product comparison identifies the tests for quasi-compactness in [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Thus quasi-compactness of space morphisms is invariant. Their relative diagonal is $a\mapsto(a,a)$, and its target fibre product is identified by that same comparison. Applying the quasi-compactness assertion to this diagonal proves invariance of quasi-separatedness of space morphisms.

source.place: Tags 03I4 and 04SG; spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 03HE and 03HL(3) as recorded in def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism

proof.text: For $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$, step 5 identifies the target of $\Delta_f$ and its map $x\mapsto(x,x,\mathrm{id})$ in both bases [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Every absolute scheme test of this target inherits its $S$-structure. Its $2$-base change of $\Delta_f$ is the identical relative fibre groupoid by step 5. Being an algebraic space over that test scheme is independent of the description of the base; the space equivalence of [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] also gives this identification. Step 7 identifies quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of the resulting space projection. The representability and both properties in the definition of a quasi-separated stack morphism therefore hold in exactly the same cases. This proves the remaining assertion of clause (3). The final product and absolute-diagonal sentences of the statement now denote the ordinary constructions on $j_!\mathcal X$; they impose no separation condition on $S$.

source.place: Tag 04YW (definition-separated), clause (4), using the explicit fibre-product comparison
